summary: Indiana requires a working smoke detector in every home at all times, but nothing in the law is triggered by selling - and a home cannot even be inspected for alarm compliance without the owner's or occupant's permission.
alarmType: At least one functional smoke detector, meaning a device that senses visible or invisible particles of combustion and meets National Fire Protection Association minimum standards for type, components and maintenance. It must be installed per the manufacturer's instructions, outside each sleeping area in the immediate vicinity of the bedrooms, on the ceiling or on a wall 4 to 12 inches below the ceiling (never recessed into the ceiling), and on each additional story including basements, cellars and habitable attics. In a split-level home with no door between levels, one on the upper level covers a lower level less than a full story below. Detectors may be battery operated or hardwired - Indiana does not require a sealed 10-year battery or interconnection in a dwelling - and must be accessible for servicing and testing. The occupant must test each one at least once every six months. A fully sprinklered building (to the Uniform Building Code standard in force when it was built) is exempt from the chapter.
certification: Nobody certifies anything at sale, and the statute actively limits inspection: except for common areas shared by three or more dwellings, a dwelling may not be inspected solely to check smoke detector compliance unless the owner or occupant gives permission. The owner, or the owner's manager or rental agent, is responsible for installing a required detector and for replacing or repairing one within seven working days of written notice. Violating the dwelling section is a Class D infraction, with separate landlord penalties. Evidence of a violation goes to the county prosecuting attorney.
citation: Ind. Code 22-11-18 (Smoke Detection Devices), especially ss 22-11-18-1, -2, -3.5, -5, -5.5, -6
